t: Born into slavery in Maryland and left with lifelong seizures and visions by an overseer's blow, Tubman escaped to Philadelphia in 1849 and went back again and again to bring out her family and others.

Known as "Moses", she rescued some 70 people in about 13 missions on the Underground Railroad, and in the Civil War she served the Union as a nurse, scout and spy, guiding the Combahee River raid of 1863.
She spent her last decades poor in Auburn, New York, campaigning for women's suffrage and caring for the old and needy, and after her death she became an American icon of courage and freedom.
dyk: Tubman began her escapes on Saturday evenings, because newspapers would not print runaway notices until Monday morning.
ev: Born Araminta Ross into slavery in Dorchester County, Maryland
Escapes from slavery to Philadelphia, travelling by night with the help of the Underground Railroad
Guides her niece Kessiah and Kessiah's children to Philadelphia in the year of the Fugitive Slave Act
Leads her aging parents north to St. Catharines, Canada
Meets John Brown and helps him plan and recruit supporters for his raid on Harpers Ferry
Guides the Union raid on the Combahee River, which carries more than 750 enslaved people to freedom
Gives the keynote speech at the first conference of the National Federation of Afro-American Women
Dies of pneumonia in Auburn, New York, and is buried with semi-military honours

f.born: c. March 1822 in Dorchester County, Maryland, into slavery, as Araminta "Minty" Ross; daughter of Harriet ("Rit") Green and Ben Ross, enslaved by the Brodess and Thompson families
f.died: 10 March 1913, of pneumonia, in Auburn, New York, surrounded by friends and family; buried with semi-military honours at Fort Hill Cemetery in Auburn
f.role: Conductor on the Underground Railroad (1850s); cook, nurse, scout and spy for the Union Army (1862–1865); suffragist; founder of the Harriet Tubman Home for the Aged in Auburn
f.known: her escape from slavery in 1849; some 13 rescue missions into Maryland; the name "Moses"; her help to John Brown before the raid on Harpers Ferry; the Combahee River raid of 1863; her work for women's suffrage; the Harriet Tubman Home for the Aged
